answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each identity to post a time-locked bond of valuable tokens that is only released after sustained honest participation. Attackers who try to flood the network with fake agents must lock up capital proportional to the number of identities they create, raising the financial cost of a large-scale attack. Honest agents can use the shared ledger as an anchor while they wander through different tasks, and a reputation bridge lets peers cross-check activity patterns before accepting new participants.
